label: Q01
question: Many casts in erdCalCOFINOAAhydros appear to be the same casts as CalCOFI's own SIO CTD/bottle casts (same station, within minutes), e.g. most of 2004-01 David Starr Jordan and 2005-01 / 2005-04 New Horizon. Are those the same physical casts, uncalibrated, with the calibrated version in the SIO CalCOFI CTD and bottle data? Is anything in them not in the SIO data?
context: Checked 2026-10-06 on a sample of casts against release v2026.10.05 (calcofi.io/db-query): e.g. 18 of 19 sampled 2004-01 JD casts match a calcofi_ctd-cast cast at the same position within 0.1 h, and 13 of 13 sampled 2005-01 NH casts match a calcofi_bottle cast within 0.3 h; NOAA-only cruises (e.g. 2003-07 and 2004-07 FRosti, 2008-04 Miller Freeman off the Pacific Northwest) match nothing. The ingest holds out every NOAA cast that has a CalCOFI cast at the same site_key within 6 h and publishes only the rest (counts per cruise in the notebook).
proposed_answer: Yes: on CalCOFI cruises these are the same casts, and the calibrated SIO versions are the record. Publish only the casts CalCOFI does not already have.

label: Q02
question: Some values look like sensor artefacts. (a) Surface (0 m) salinity is below 30 PSU on 101 of 447 surface readings, many far offshore and far too low to be real (e.g. 2004-01 JD order 25, line 90 station 37: 1.57 PSU; 2013-04 OS order 78: 0.48 PSU). (b) On 2012-04 Ocean Starr, eight casts (order 61-86, lines 71.5-80, stations 60-111) read 0.2-6.1 degC throughout and oxygen up to 14.9 ml/L, which is not possible off central California in April. Should these be excluded, or is there a quality flag we should use?
context: All of these lie inside the registry's bounds (salinity_1 0-45 PSU, temperature_1 -2 to 40 degC, oxygen_ml_l_1 0-15 ml/L), so the ingest publishes them as-is for now. The source has no quality flag column. Low surface salinity near the coast north of the CalCOFI grid (e.g. 29-30 PSU off Oregon and Washington) is plausible (river plumes) and is not part of this question.

label: Q03
question: ERDDAP says oxygen and salinity are 'mostly uncalibrated'. Which casts or cruises are calibrated, and is the temperature on the ITS-90 scale?
context: The ingest publishes every value under the uncorrected-sensor measurement types (temperature_1, salinity_1, oxygen_ml_l_1). If some cruises are calibrated, they could be published as calibrated values instead.

context: citation_main and doi are empty. The ERDDAP .das gives institution "NOAA SWFSC", title "CalCOFI NOAA Additional CTD" and publisher Ed Weber, but no citation string or DOI. Checked 2026-10-06. Same gap as swfsc_cufes Q06.
proposed_answer: NOAA Fisheries, Southwest Fisheries Science Center. CalCOFI NOAA Additional CTD. NOAA CoastWatch ERDDAP erdCalCOFINOAAhydros. (No DOI.)

label: Q05
question: percent_saturation is filled on 5 cruises only (4,963 of 15,151 rows). Is it computed from the CTD oxygen, temperature and salinity, or measured separately?
context: Not published: it is sparse, and if it is computed it can be derived from the published values. Checked 2026-10-06 on all 4,963 values: 100 x oxygen / O2 solubility (Garcia & Gordon 1992, ml/L) from the same row's temperature and salinity reproduces percent_saturation with a median ratio of 0.9998 and within 0.2 percentage points for 99% of rows.
proposed_answer: Computed: oxygen as a percent of its saturation at the sample's temperature and salinity (Garcia & Gordon 1992 solubility). Not a separate measurement, so it stays unpublished.
